name: Hemolytic Vapor Induction Carbine
description:
The HVIC-3 operates by projecting a tuned aerosol of catalytic nanoparticles into the breathing zone of a target, where they are subsequently activated by a focused near-infrared trigger pulse from the carbine's secondary emitter. Once inhaled or absorbed transdermally, the particles bind to hemoglobin iron sites and initiate a controlled oxidative cascade, forcing red blood cells into a premature lysis cycle. The effect begins within ninety seconds of exposure and manifests as rapidly progressing hypoxia, subcutaneous hemorrhaging, and systemic pressure collapse. Range is limited to approximately eighteen meters in open air, though enclosed spaces dramatically amplify dispersal efficiency.

What separates the HVIC-3 from cruder aerosol weapons is its selectivity system. Operators can pre-load a biometric exclusion profile — a genetic or proteomic signature — allowing the carbine to suppress activation in targeted individuals while the cloud remains lethal to everyone else in the zone. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric markets this as a 'precision population management tool,' which has done little to soften the weapon's reputation. The carbine itself resembles an oversized pump-action shotgun with a bulbous canister housing beneath the barrel, and emits a faint copper smell during discharge that veteran operators have learned to treat as a serious warning sign.

The nickname 'Redmist' comes not from the aerosol itself, which is invisible, but from the subcutaneous hemorrhaging that gives affected skin a mottled crimson flush in the final stages of exposure. 'The Blush' is used more sardonically, typically by the corporate security contractors who deploy it for crowd suppression in sealed transit hubs and processing centers.
specifications:
effective range: 18m open air / 40m enclosed
canister capacity: 6 discharge cycles per canister
activation delay: 90 seconds post-exposure
exclusion profiles: Up to 4 simultaneous biometric exemptions
weight: 4.2 kg loaded
dimensions: 74cm length
power source: Integrated DAT cell, 30 trigger pulses per charge
tactical_use: Deployed almost exclusively in enclosed or semi-enclosed environments where aerosol dispersal is predictable. Operators typically seed a space, withdraw, and trigger activation remotely after establishing a perimeter. The exclusion profile system makes it viable for extractions where a target must survive while everyone else in the room does not. Counter-use involves positive-pressure respirators and full dermal sealing, though the near-infrared trigger can sometimes be blocked by certain optical coatings.
cultural_context: The HVIC-3 exists in a strange public silence — it is widely known among intelligence communities and black-site operators but almost never discussed openly, partly because Zheng-Dao Bioelectric aggressively suppresses documentation of its use. Among corporate fixers, possession of one is considered a statement of institutional backing rather than personal capability. Street operators who come across one typically sell it immediately; the legal exposure is catastrophic and the weapon's use leaves forensic evidence that is difficult to misattribute.
known_users: GLMZ Sanitation Authority internal affairs division (unconfirmed)
story_hooks: A transit hub massacre leaves 40 dead with no visible wounds and no weapon recovered — only a faint copper smell in the ventilation system and one survivor with an inexplicable genetic exemption.
A stolen exclusion profile cartridge is being auctioned on the black market, pre-loaded with a biometric signature that nobody can identify but everyone wants.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric is recalling all HVIC-3 units through a shell contractor — but the recall notices are only going to operators who used the weapon in a specific six-month window, and those operators are going missing.
An operator is hired to protect a VIP, only to discover mid-mission that the client's biometric profile is not in the exclusion cartridge they were issued.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist bioweapon masquerading as industrial equipment. The HVIC-3 reads as a heavily modified pump-action carbine with a pronounced, bulbous lower receiver that dominates the weapon's visual center of gravity. The overall impression is aggressive and medical simultaneously—a thing designed to dispense invisible death with the ergonomic familiarity of a shotgun. Its silhouette is chunky, purposeful, unapologetically utilitarian.
physical_description.dimensions: 74 cm overall length; bulbous canister housing extends 12 cm beneath the barrel; upper receiver width approximately 5 cm; stock-to-muzzle depth creates a compact but dense profile
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and front-weighted. At 4.2 kg loaded, the carbine feels anchored by the canister—not unwieldy, but demanding respect and deliberate handling. The mass sits forward, requiring proper stance.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade aluminum chassis with reinforced titanium canister vessel. The receiver is reinforced carbon-composite polymer with integrated thermal management vents. Secondary emitter assembly is surgical-grade stainless steel.
physical_description.finish: Brushed gunmetal gray with clinical precision. The canister housing features a matte anodized finish that resists fingerprints. Selective areas—trigger guard, magazine well, emitter ports—show a slightly darker, almost blackened treatment suggesting repeated exposure to near-infrared discharge residue.
physical_description.color_scheme: Institutional gray-silver primary with gunmetal accents. The canister displays faint amber-tinted indicator windows along its length. Secondary emitter aperture has a subtle copper glow when powered.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured rubberized polymer wrap in dark charcoal, providing secure purchase even through light exposure suits. The grip is ergonomic but deliberately utilitarian—no comfort, only control.
distinctive_features: Bulbous crystalline-look canister housing with internal visible particulate suspension (faintly opalescent under light)
Amber LED indicator strip running the length of the canister showing charge/load status
Secondary near-infrared emitter array recessed into the upper receiver, visible as a cluster of tiny dark ports
Pressure relief vents along the canister sides, aesthetically resembling industrial cooling fins
Biometric exclusion profile interface—a small palm-print scanner mounted on the right side of the receiver
Subtle copper-colored oxidation rings around muzzle end from aerosol discharge residue
Mechanical safety lever positioned for right-hand operation, marked with warning glyphs in ZHENG-DAO corporate red
Power indicator—faint blue LED beneath the rear sight mount
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC corporate logo (stylized DNA helix) stamped in matte on the upper receiver near the rear. Serial plate mounted on the left side of the canister in raised characters. Technical specifications and biohazard warnings etched below the canister in multiple languages. A small red warning triangle with the company symbol appears near the muzzle.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-maintained but never pristine. The brushed finish shows micro-scratches from regular disassembly and cleaning. Slight discoloration around the secondary emitter ports from repeated activation. No rust or deep scarring—this is a weapon kept in working condition by contractors who understand its lethality. The canister may show faint particulate settling or residual opalescence from repeated fills.
